page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge belongs to the compute-optimized instance tier, utilizing the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The virtual machine runs on an arm64 AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It offers 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory measures 8.0 GB, supplying 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes hardware AES acceleration but lacks x86 vector instruction sets. There is no bundled local storage, meaning primary persistence relies on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Synthetic testing demonstrates consistent mid-tier performance across common compute and memory metrics. Under stress-ng, the instance achieves scores of 1532.39 in single-core and 6112.46 in multi-core tests. Geekbench evaluation matches this pattern, recording 1523.0 for single-core and 5029.0 for multi-core, with Clang software compilation reaching 6289.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 386.35 GB/s on cached 16 KB read workloads, while uncached 256 MB read and write streams achieve 107.79 GB/s and 39.43 GB/s, respectively. Application benchmarks show 6.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.15 GB/s of static web serving throughput. Lower results appear in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 28.42 GB/s, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and ray tracing. Large language model inference yields 65.88 tokens per second on small models and 6.51 tokens per second on 7B models.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile presents an architecture engineered for compute-focused and network-oriented services rather than memory-heavy databases. With 12 Gbps of baseline network throughput, resource efficiency is pronounced in scenarios demanding high network throughput per compute core without requiring local disk operations. The absence of local NVMe storage represents a clear operational tradeoff, necessitating network-attached storage integration for any persistent disk operations. Overall, the server fits web serving, software building pipelines, packet processing, network appliances, and Redis caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System and powered by a 2.6 GHz AWS Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processor. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, delivering 4 vCPUs paired with 8.0 GB of memory for a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached storage via EBS, while offering a 12 Gbps baseline network capability. Synthetic performance benchmarks indicate average results across standard stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core operations, alongside 6.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.15 GB/s in static web throughput. Lower performance appears in multi-threaded decompression, ray tracing, PassMark CPU suites, and LLM text generation tasks. With its elevated baseline network bandwidth and ARM architecture, the c7gn.xlarge fits network-intensive utilities, static web serving, caching tiers, and software compilation tasks.
